title: Meeting preparation note — 17 June
text:
Prepare for separate discretionary distribution decisions for the Alder Quay Settlement and the Flint Orchard Settlement, in that order. Use the administered records held at 16:00 BST on 12 June 2026. For each settlement, distinguish who may be considered from what has already been authorised for payment, and note anything the trustees should check before deciding.

I have booked one slot on 17 June with Nell Carvane and Tobin Rell. The appointments book shows both in office for both settlements, with no change entered since the deeds were lodged.

**Alder Quay Settlement — first working paper and minute entry.** Use the lodged deed to identify who may be considered. List any payments already authorised separately, with a reference to the recorded decision for each. Flag anything the trustees need to confirm under the deed or reconcile with the decision and payment records before deciding.

**Flint Orchard Settlement — second working paper and minute entry.** Make the same checks against Flint Orchard’s own deed and records. Keep its list of those who may be considered, its recorded payment authorisations and its points for confirmation separate from Alder Quay’s.

List unresolved ordinary finance queries separately from the decision papers. Send any late papers separately to the meeting; do not add them to the closed preparation set. This note authorises no payment.

Maren Dovell  
Meeting Secretary, Brindlewick Trust Office  
12 June 2026

title: Alder Quay Settlement — certified deed extract
text:
BRINDLEWICK TRUST OFFICE
ALDER QUAY SETTLEMENT — CERTIFIED SELECTED-CLAUSE EXTRACT

To: Kit Wenslow, Tarnstile Advisory
Deed date: 21 October 2022
Lodged parent deed reference: PD-6834-R
Settlor: Ellis Harnett
Original trustees: Nell Carvane and Tobin Rell

3. Original discretionary objects
The original discretionary objects are Ione Berrick and Emmett Vann.

4. Discretion over income and capital
The trustees exercise their discretion over income and capital jointly. No object is entitled to a payment before an appointment is made in that object’s favour.

6. Addition of discretionary objects
The trustees for the time being may, acting unanimously and without the settlor’s consent, add by deed any named living individual other than the settlor or a serving trustee. The designation takes effect on joint delivery as a deed.

Where the trustees use the common deed custody service, they may identify the settlement at delivery by jointly stating its lodged parent reference and associating that reference with the unique reference written on the designation. The settlement name need not appear in the designation. The custodian only memorialises delivery.

Existing objects remain unless separately removed by deed.

9. Governing law
The law of England and Wales applies.

— Schedule omitted from this extract —

I certify that I checked this selected-clause extract against the lodged Alder Quay Settlement deed, parent deed reference PD-6834-R, and that it accurately sets out the provisions identified above.

Tess Arnay
Deed-records clerk, Brindlewick Trust Office
9 June 2026

title: Flint Orchard Settlement — certified deed extract
text:
Brindlewick Trust Office
Certified deed extract

To: Kit Wenslow, Tarnstile Advisory

Settlement: Flint Orchard Settlement
Deed date: 21 October 2022
Lodged parent deed reference: PD-6894-R
Settlor: Cora Teague
Original trustees: Nell Carvane and Tobin Rell

Clause 2 — Objects
The named Objects are Ione Berrick and Orla Penrick.

Clause 5 — Income and capital
The trustees act together in exercising their discretionary power over income and capital. They may apply funds directly for an Object’s benefit. Eligibility alone creates no right to payment.

Clause 8 — Addition of Objects
All serving trustees, acting together, may by deed add any named living individual other than the settlor or a serving trustee. No other person’s consent is required.

An addition takes effect when the trustees jointly deliver the designation as a deed. On delivery through the common custody service, the trustees may identify the settlement by giving its lodged parent deed reference against the unique reference written on the designation. The settlement name need not be written on the designation. The register records the delivery, not the designation.

Existing Objects remain Objects unless separately removed by deed.

Clause 12 — Governing law
The law of England and Wales applies.

I certify that I have checked this extract against the lodged parent deed. Schedules are not reproduced.

Bram Lerrit
Deed-records clerk, Brindlewick Trust Office
9 June 2026

title: Merefold deed accession register — certified single-entry extract
text:
MEREFOLD DEED SERVICES  
Certified single-entry extract from the live custody register

To: Brindlewick Trust Office, for onward supply to its adviser

Entry transcription

Instrument reference: SD-Q7M2  
Parent deed reference: PD-6894-R

At 11:30 GMT on 26 March 2026, Nell Carvane and Tobin Rell attended together and released one signed paper original for immediate delivery as a deed, not in escrow. At handover, both confirmed the parent deed reference against the instrument reference on the face of the paper. I made the register entry from that handover, not from a trust-title search or a beneficiary file, and placed the original in the common deed vault that day.

Office conventions and officer explanation

The custody classification records receipt of one signed paper original released for immediate delivery as a deed, rather than held in escrow. It records one original, not a numbered counterpart series. Instrument references are labels drawn from a shared stock; they do not identify a trust or indicate a sequence.

A question mark in a reference field on an issued copy stands for a character the officer cannot read or reproduce from the available source. It is not a literal reference character and does not certify any inferred character.

I certify that this extract is a true extract of this entry only from Merefold Deed Services’ live register.

Gideon Sarn  
Custody Officer, Merefold Deed Services  
11 June 2026

title: Letter from Ione Berrick about future expenses
text:
18 February

Nell Carvane and Tobin Rell  
c/o Brindlewick Trust Office

Dear Nell and Tobin,

You asked me to let you know if the replacement travel estimate came in before summer. It hasn’t come in yet, and the old estimate is no longer reliable. Sella Quist helps me keep track of envelopes and chase paperwork, and she has my permission to pass the new estimate on to you when it arrives. I’ll sign anything you need me to confirm myself.

Sella has turned down shifts to help me. Would you consider whether you can help her in her own right, if you think that’s appropriate? I don’t know what either deed allows. I’m not asking for a standing payment, for any payment meant for me to go to Sella, or for anything to be deducted from a payment to me.

I know Sella paid for a few copies or stamps herself. I’d expect those expenses to be accounted for separately.

Yours sincerely,

Ione Berrick

title: EX-K4 — office expense reconciliation
text:
Brindlewick Trust Office  
11 June — Expense reconciliation: EX-K4  
For the Trustees’ records desk and adviser pack compiler  
Prepared by Una Cresset, Accounts Administrator

Sella Quist submitted £12.60 for postage and £8.40 for print-shop charges for getting Ione Berrick’s papers to the office.

Postage — £12.60 reimbursed. The postage slip was attached to the claim. I matched the reimbursement on 5 June to the office operating account line marked EX-K4.

Print-shop charges — £8.40 remains a query. My expense list refers to the receipt, but the office did not receive it and has no copy or substitute voucher on file. The amount has not been paid and is not an authorised balance.

The office has not recharged either item. The remit entry names Sella Quist as payee and queries contact for EX-K4 only. I hold no distribution instruction for this claim.
